title: UK Lays New Sanctions Regulations Targeting Iran's Financial System, Bans Iranian Aircraft
detail: Foreign Office Minister Stephen Doughty laid 'The Iran (Sanctions) (Amendment) Regulations 2026' before Parliament, amending the UK's existing Iran sanctions regimes and going beyond the UN snapback measures the UK implemented on October 1, 2025. The new regulations restrict Iran's access to the UK financial system and its ability to raise funds, expand trade prohibitions to additional goods, technology and services tied to nuclear escalation — including energy, software, metals, gold, shipping, insurance and banking — and ban Iranian aircraft from landing in the UK, with limited exemptions. The statement also expands UK powers to sanction ships facilitating Iran's nuclear program. Doughty said the measures 'double down on our action to constrain Iran's nuclear ambitions,' citing Iran's roughly 400 kg stockpile enriched to 60% as unparalleled among non-nuclear-weapons states. The measures take effect September 29, 2026, and include a general licence preserving Azerbaijan's Shah Deniz gas field operations, in line with EU and US policy.

media.caption: The UK laid new legislation expanding sanctions on Iran's financial system and banning Iranian aircraft

title: 'No to Execution Tuesdays' Campaign Marks 137th Week as Executions Since Late August Top 45
detail: Prisoners across 62 facilities nationwide — including Qezel Hesar, Evin, Karaj Central, Qarchak and regional prisons — marked the 137th consecutive week of the 'No to Execution Tuesdays' campaign with coordinated hunger strikes protesting the accelerating pace of state executions. The campaign's statement said at least 11 individuals were hanged in the preceding week alone, bringing the total recorded since August 23 to more than 45. The statement highlighted the cases of Ali Zarei, a 2022-protest eye-injury survivor facing a death sentence, and Erfan Mirzaei, a political prisoner who died under suspicious circumstances in Dastgerd Prison, Isfahan, alongside a group of ten protesters sentenced to death plus 11 years each. The campaign called for international solidarity and intervention from human rights organizations.
confidenceReason: Reported directly by the prisoner-led campaign via an opposition-aligned human rights monitor; not independently corroborated by wire services given restricted access to Iranian prisons.
